Company: 
Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. 
 Job Area: 
Engineering Group, Engineering Group > CPU Engineering 
 General Summary: 
 About the Role   

   

   You will contribute to a Python-based random test generation (RTG) framework and its companion assembler library that together form the   core of a RISC-V CPU design-verification toolchain. The RTG drives a   JIT-style, simulator- coupled generator that produces ELF binaries   exercising the RVA23.1 ISA — including privileged modes, virtual   memory, interrupts, vector, and cryptography extensions. The   assembler library provides the bit-accurate instruction encoding   

   layer that the RTG and other tools consume.   

   

   What You'll Do   

   

  Implement new generation objects for RISC-V extensions; common   micro-architectural scenarios; and complex data/control-flow   composable idioms.   
 
 Add instruction forms and encodings to the python companion   assembler and verifying bit-level correctness against the RISC-V   ISA spec.   
 
 Write and tune generation themes which are knob-driven test   profiles that compose objects to improve RTL coverage.   
 
 Work within the privileged-software stack: exception/interrupt   handlers, page-table builders, PMP configuration, and IMSIC programming sequences.   
 
  Work with ISS and RTL verification engineers to triage failures,   add targeted regression scenarios, and adjust constraint logic   (register allocators, address-space managers, data fillers).   
 
   

   What We're Looking For   

   

  2–5 years of experience in CPU design verification, ISS   development, or hardware-software co-design.   
 
 Solid Python 3 skills; comfort with generator-based coroutines and object- oriented design patterns.   
 
  Working knowledge of the RISC-V ISA: instruction encoding formats  ( R/I/S/B/ U/J, compressed, vector), CSR semantics, privilege   levels (M/S/U), and the memory model.   Alternatively, similar knowledge for x86 or ARM.   
 
 Familiarity with virtual memory (Sv39/Sv48), PMP, and   trap/interrupt handling.   
 
 Exposure to random test generation flows or ISS/RTL co-simulation   is a plus.   
 
   

   Nice to Have   

   Compiler development experience.   
 
 Understanding of hypervisor and/or AIA/IMSIC interrupt   architecture.   
 
 Familiarity with constraint-propagation libraries. 
 
 
 Minimum Qualifications: 
• Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field and 4+ years of Hardware Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related work experience.
 OR
Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field and 3+ years of Hardware Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related work experience.
 OR
PhD in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or related field and 2+ years of Hardware Engineering, Software Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or related work experience.
